newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Kim says to provide $350,000 to Pyongyang.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Kim says to provide $350,000 to Pyongyang.

text.p: South Korea's President Kim Young-sam vowed to provide $350,000 to North Korea to help reconstruct a rehydration salt plant damaged by the floods in 1995, the domestic Yonhap news agency said on Sunday.
Kim, who is visiting Chile as part of a tour to Latin America, made the remarks at a dinner with South Korea's top business leaders, including Hyundai Group chairman Chung Mong-ku.
"I would like to provide the aid to the North on a humanitarian basis through the U.N. Children's Fund," Kim was quoted as saying.

South Korea shipped $1 million worth of powdered milk to North Korea in August as part of a relief effort to ease child malnutrition stemming from food shortages in the Stalinist nation. The milk was part of $3 million in relief aid the Seoul government had pledged for North Korea.
In July, South Korea gave $2 million to the United Nations World Food Programme to buy grain powder after the U.N. appealed for $43.6 million to help ease the effects of floods in the North.
Millions of North Koreans are believed to face hunger because of the floods, according to international aid agencies.
